note: PRODUCTION-RATE derived corpus. Provenance: reference corpus scenarios.json (schemaVersion 1, dt=1/60). Production fixed step is 1/120 in BOTH engines (js/main.js:1217 FIXED_STEP=1/120; godot match_controller.gd:66 FIXED_STEP=1/120). 1/60 is the REFERENCE corpus tick, never a production fixed tick. Each frame carries its own render-frame `delta` (seconds). Full-step deltas are one ULP ABOVE 1/120 (0.008333333333333334) so both engines' IEEE doubles run the step unambiguously (the exact 18-digit decimal 0.008333333333333333 rounds 1 ulp BELOW GDScript's 1.0/120.0 and would eat a frame).

scenarios.description: No button, neutral sticks, five full-step frames. Baseline: nothing queues.
A pressed one full-step frame, released the next. POSITIVE CONTROL: release lands on a 1-substep frame, both engines must queue a drive.
A held 12 full-step frames (0.1s at 1/120), then released. Partial charge accrual.
RB + A held together 6 frames, released. technicalModifier -> chiquita.
A held while left stick pushed; release captures curved aim.
60 Hz render (delta 1/60 = 2 sub-steps per frame). CONTROL: release on a 2-substep frame, both engines queue.

240 Hz render (delta 1/240): A pressed, held one frame (1 substep), released on a frame with ZERO sub-steps. Genuine physical A press/hold/release timeline, NOT hit=true injected. THE DISCRIMINATOR: browser clears the one-shot in getInput() before the accumulator; Godot latches it and delivers on the next sub-step.

144 Hz render (delta 1/144): A held 5 frames then released on a zero-substep frame (the 0/1 substep alternation at 144 Hz lands the release on a 0-step frame). Secondary 144 Hz instance of the same divergence.
